name: Arcturus GL-6 'Sermon'
description:
A rotary-cylinder grenade launcher holding six 40mm rounds, built with the overengineered brutality that characterizes all Arcturus ordnance. The GL-6 uses a clockwork-style mechanical action — no electronics, no batteries, no firmware to hack. Each cylinder position accepts any standard 40mm casing, allowing operators to load mixed payloads: fragmentation, incendiary, smoke, flashbang, and chemical in whatever combination the situation demands. The weapon's nickname 'Sermon' derives from the practice of loading all six cylinders with different munition types — operators call it 'preaching the full gospel.'

The GL-6's mechanical simplicity makes it the preferred launcher for operations in EMP-hardened environments or against targets with electronic warfare capability. While competitors have introduced smart-linked launchers with programmable airburst and guided munitions, the Sermon continues to outsell them in actual combat deployments because it always works. No boot sequence, no calibration, no network dependency. Point it at the problem and pull the trigger six times.
legality: Military — restricted deployment authorization; widely available on black market
specifications:
caliber: 40mm standard casings
cylinder capacity: 6 rounds
effective range: 50-400 meters (munition dependent)
muzzle velocity: 76 m/s
weight: 6.2 kg unloaded
length: 680mm
action: Double-action mechanical rotary
tactical_use: Area denial, fortification clearance, mixed-threat engagement. Operators typically load alternating fragmentation and incendiary rounds for urban combat, or smoke and flashbang for extraction operations. The six-round capacity allows sustained suppression without reloading during short engagements.
cultural_context: The GL-6 has become iconic in GLMZ's mercenary culture. Freelance operators who carry one are making a statement about their willingness to escalate — grenades are not subtle, and deploying them in urban environments guarantees collateral damage. Carrying a Sermon means you've decided that precision is less important than results.
known_users: GLMZ Tactical Response heavy weapons squads
Several Shelf district militias (black market units)
story_hooks: A cache of GL-6 launchers has been seized with cylinders pre-loaded with an unknown 40mm round that doesn't match any cataloged munition type. The rounds are heavier than standard and their casings are warm to the touch.

Someone has been firing GL-6 incendiary rounds into abandoned buildings in the Shelf — not randomly, but targeting specific structures. Each building burned contained evidence of something someone wanted destroyed.
related_entities: Street Custom 'Sunday School' Weaponized Religious Artifact

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist mechanical beast — a chunky, industrial rotary grenade launcher with the deliberate overbuilt aesthetic of a Cold War relic crossed with near-future pragmatism. The visible cylinder dominates the profile, a hexagonal drum that speaks to reliable simplicity. Compact and purposeful, with no unnecessary curves or smoothing.
physical_description.dimensions: 680mm overall length, 220mm cylinder diameter, 110mm width across the stock. Cylinder rotates flush with the receiver.
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial and reassuring in hand — 6.2kg unloaded feels dense but balanced. The recoil stock shifts weight forward slightly, making it feel deliberately designed for controlled aggression rather than finesse.
physical_description.primary_material: Blackened steel cylinder and barrel, reinforced aluminum alloy receiver, composite polymer furniture. Internal mechanisms are hardened steel — visible through inspection ports as dark mechanical detail.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal black with deliberate machine-marks visible on the cylinder. The barrel shows faint tool marks and wear patterns. Polymer handguard is textured matte black with light scratch marks suggesting field use.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal black primary with brushed steel accent highlights on the cylinder firing pin, trigger guard in dull chrome, and orange safety indicator ring (40mm-standard marking).
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized pistol grip with deep checkering for wet/gloved operation. The forestock is wrapped textured polymer with subtle diamond pattern. Metal surfaces around the trigger are smooth, worn shiny from regular handling.
distinctive_features: Visible hexagonal cylinder with six numbered position marks (1-6) engraved in white
Mechanical double-action trigger with substantial travel distance
Spring-loaded cylinder rotation detent with audible click at each position
Top-mounted iron sight bracket with protected aperture
Vented cooling slots along the barrel jacket
Open breech inspection port showing internal mechanical linkages
Recoil-dampening stock with pneumatic buffer visible as dual cylinders
Ammunition loading guide etched along the top rail
Worn manual safety lever (forward: fire, rear: safe) in dull brass
Faint laser-etched serial plate on the left receiver face
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Blackwood Commercial Group logo (stylized arrow) stamped on the left receiver. Model designation 'GL-6' and 'SERMON' engraved in small caps below the cylinder. Serial number and manufacturing date (2224 or 2225) on the lower receiver plate, partially obscured by use.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but clearly used. The black finish shows micro-scratches from field handling, dust residue in the mechanical recesses, light carbon scoring around the muzzle. The safety lever shows shine-wear from repeated manipulation. No visible rust or corrosion — this is a weapon that gets regular care despite heavy deployment.
